This decentralized architecture was originally perceived as legally safer because the actual copyrighted files were stored on individual users' computers rather than on a central server.", "summary": "The BitTorrent protocol uses decentralized metadata to direct users to peers, avoiding centralized file hosting."}, "3": {"original": "Files are not hosted on a centralised server but on users' computers.", "rephrased": "Unlike centralized file sharing systems, the BitTorrent protocol stores actual files directly on the computers of individual users rather than on a central server, relying instead on a network of peers to share and verify data. This distributed storage model was initially viewed as a significant legal advantage, as it theoretically reduced the liability of the service provider compared to hosting all content on a single point of failure.", "summary": "BitTorrent stores files on users' computers rather than a central server, offering a legal advantage."}}
